title: Make the promise feel like the prospect's own identity.
dek: In the identification technique, Eugene Schwartz studies a second kind of desire: not only the urge to get something, but the longing to become, express, or recognize oneself through the product.

marginNote.label: Apprenticeship Note
marginNote.body: A desire becomes more powerful when the prospect can see the desired self inside the promise. The product is no longer only a solution; it becomes a way to express who the buyer is trying to be.

canon.heading: Schwartz: give the promise a self the prospect can recognize.
canon.standfirst: Read Part II, Chapter 8, "The Second Technique of Breakthrough Copy: Identification," from Eugene Schwartz's Breakthrough Advertising on PDF pages 115-132. Schwartz moves beyond desire as appetite and studies the quieter longing to express, inhabit, or become a particular kind of person.
canon.readerIntro: Read this as a study of identity entering the sale. Mark where Schwartz distinguishes wanting a result from wanting the self-image associated with that result, where the product becomes a vehicle for expression, and where the copywriter must make that identity concrete without relying on empty status language. Then map one offer: the current self, the desired self, the social proof, and the product behavior that lets the prospect cross the distance.

blocks.label: 01 / Desire is also a longing for expression
paragraphs: Schwartz begins by separating obvious desire from a subtler motive: the prospect may not only want satisfaction or relief, but a way to express a self that is not yet fully visible in ordinary life.

That makes identification different from a decorative persona. The copy is working with a psychological movement from who the prospect feels they are now toward who they want to recognize in themselves.

blocks.label: 02 / The product becomes a vehicle for a self-image
paragraphs: The identification technique gives the product a role inside the prospect's imagined identity. It can become evidence of taste, competence, belonging, independence, refinement, courage, or another personally meaningful quality.
The important question is not which adjective the brand wants to own. It is what the buyer wants the act of choosing, using, or possessing the product to say about them.

blocks.label: 03 / The desired identity must feel attainable
paragraphs: An identity claim fails when it is too remote from the prospect's lived situation. Schwartz's examples point toward a bridge: a recognizable person, scene, role, or behavior that lets the buyer imagine entering the desired identity without pretending to become someone else overnight.
This is why the surrounding details matter. The image, setting, language, and user must make the identity feel available, not merely admired from a distance.

blocks.label: 04 / Identification needs a product behavior to carry it
paragraphs: The product cannot be a blank badge. Its design, use, community, ritual, or result must give the identity somewhere to live. Otherwise the copy is asking language to create a transformation the experience cannot support.

Look for the connection between the imagined self and the product's actual performance. The strongest identity promise is reinforced every time the product is used in the way the prospect hopes to be seen using it.

blocks.label: 05 / The copywriter builds the bridge between self and choice
paragraphs: The practical work is to show the prospect a version of themselves that is emotionally attractive and behaviorally plausible. The ad does not merely say, 'people like you buy this'; it gives the buyer a scene in which the choice expresses something they already want to make true.
Stop with an identification map: present self, desired self, social tension, product behavior, and the scene that lets the prospect recognize the identity as their own.

closeReading: How does Schwartz distinguish the desire for satisfaction from the longing for identification?
What kind of self-image does the product allow the prospect to express, and what makes that image believable?
Where does the chapter show the difference between an identity that is admired and one that feels attainable?
Choose one offer. What is the present self, desired self, social tension, and product behavior that connects them?
Find one piece of brand language that claims identity without proving it. What experience, ritual, or scene would make the claim real?

principle.heading: Make the product a credible way to become more like the self the buyer wants to be.
principle.body: People do not buy only for the result. They also buy for the identity the choice lets them express. The promise becomes stronger when the product experience gives that identity a concrete place to live.
principle.example: A writing tool should not only promise faster drafting. It can become the instrument for the independent operator who wants to think clearly, publish consistently, and be recognized for useful judgment rather than frantic output.
principle.practice: Choose one offer and write five lines: present self, desired self, social tension, product behavior, and identity scene. Then remove any identity claim that the product's actual use cannot support.

output.heading: Give the desire a self to become.
output.body: For one offer, map the identity the buyer has, the identity they want, and the product behavior that makes the transition feel real rather than merely flattering.

fieldNotes.title: Google makes high-definition video creation part of the ordinary workspace
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Google made 1080p video generation in Google Vids available at no cost to Google Account users, with Gemini Omni controls for scene duration, transitions, and continuity, plus ready-made templates for launches and product communication.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The competitive move is not only a better model. It lowers the distance between having an idea and producing a credible visual artifact, which means the new bottleneck moves toward taste, direction, and knowing what deserves to be made.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether free creation increases the amount of mediocre video or creates a new baseline for small teams that can now test visual ideas before they hire production help.

fieldNotes.title: Target puts design memory at the center of a national campaign
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Target launched its national Inside Out campaign around its customers and iconic red shopping bags, extending the idea through broadcast, streaming, radio, digital, social, creator partnerships, and experiential activations.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The campaign treats a recognizable design asset as a working memory system rather than a logo placed on top of advertising. The same cue travels through media, merchandise, creators, and experience, making the brand easier to recognize in more buying situations.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the red-bag asset remains distinctive as it is stretched across more formats, or whether repetition without a fresh customer truth turns a memory cue into decoration.

fieldNotes.title: Amazon draws a hard line around agentic shopping
fieldNotes.whatHappened: TechCrunch reported that Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on Amazon, citing unauthorized access and the risk that the retailer would have to resolve bad orders made by an agent.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: Agentic commerce is exposing a new positioning and accountability boundary. The company that owns the transaction may not want to surrender the customer relationship or the cost of mistakes to an intermediary that acts on the buyer's behalf.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch for standards or partnerships that separate agent discovery from merchant accountability, because convenience will not scale unless someone remains clearly responsible for the outcome.

tweets.author: Sawyer Merritt
tweets.title: A product launch makes the interface part of the category
tweets.summary: This is worth carrying because it shows a new product competing through a full experience rather than a single specification. The display, puck, gestures, content partnerships, and AI are being assembled into a new way to consume media, which is exactly how a category gets redefined in the buyer's mind.
